title: Character detail screens: one template, two hero colors (Tracer and Soldier 76)
contains_third_party_content: Overwatch characters and ability names (copyrighted game IP).

observed.layout: Two phones with thick black bezels. Top: a hero block with rounded bottom corners, colored per character (orange for Tracer, blue for Soldier 76), with the character art breaking the frame and a huge white rotated name on the right edge. A white square back button top-left; 'Difficulty' with stars (two for Tracer, one for Soldier 76). Below: small pill tabs 'Overview | Story'; 'Role' and a large bold 'DAMAGE'; a short grey bio; 'Abilities' with three round icon buttons and captions (Pulse Pistols, Blink, Pulse Bomb; Helix Rockets, Sprint, Biotic Field).
observed.hierarchy: Hero art and rotated name, then the role, bio and abilities.
observed.typography: Bold geometric sans; large rotated display name; small grey bio. Typeface unconfirmed.
observed.iconography: Round ability buttons with generic glyphs; star rating.
observed.materials: Flat color block with rounded bottom corners; white lower half.

implementation_notes: Per-hero theme color on the hero block.
Rotated name via writing-mode or a CSS transform.

concept_work.essence: One template, a theme color per entity, and a fixed information order.
what_makes_it_work: The system is obvious across two skins.
The rotated name is both label and graphic.
The lower half follows the same order for both heroes.
gaps_to_make_it_work: The rotated hero name measures about 1.76:1 (white on orange).
Bio text measures about 1.83-1.98:1 and 'Difficulty' on orange about 1.24:1.
Difficulty stars show only filled stars, with no scale.
Tabs are tiny and the active state is subtle; ability icons are generic; only Overview content is shown.

links: The rotated name overlaps the art to unify them.

approach: Template with a theme variable per entity

pattern.name: Themed detail template
use_when: Many entities share a detail page but each needs its own identity (characters, products, destinations)
avoid_when: Entities have no strong identity color
adaptation_examples: Car model pages with a theme color per model.
Travel destination cards with a color per region.

lessons: Take each entity's theme color from its own art.
Give every rating a visible scale.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: One saturated color block per hero (orange, blue) with a white lower half.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: A detail template whose information order is clear.
Bold color blocks and a strong type moment.
Detail-screen conventions are met, but an unscaled rating and tiny tabs weaken correctness.
Tab state is subtle and only Overview is shown.
A known template with a strong rotated-name device.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 1.76:1; secondary text min 1.24:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

critical_failures.description: A primary text/label measures below 3:1 contrast (best estimate)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
